title: National system for domestic commercial vessel safety
summary: From 1 July 2013 one national law replaced the separate state and territory regimes for commercial vessels, with AMSA as the national regulator. From 1 July 2018 AMSA also took over day-to-day services from the states, so vessel certificates and crew qualifications are national.

instruments.title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law Act 2012
instruments.provisions: sections 3 to 19 and Schedule 1 (the National Law)

direction_rationale: A single national law lets commercial vessels and crew operate in any state's waters under one set of certificates and one regulator.

verified.notes: Assent and commencement (1 July 2013, F2013L00607) from section 2 of the Act as made. AMSA's service delivery date (1 July 2018) is from AMSA's domestic commercial vessels page.

assessment.summary: One national vessel safety law and regulator replaced eight state regimes, so operators and crew can work across state waters without separate certificates.

marks.reason: Vessels and crew certified once can operate in any state's waters.
Operators deal with one regulator for surveys, certificates and permits.
